acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Stores tab button appears first in the Configuration tab bar.
The default active tab remains 'general' (not changed to 'stores').
Clicking the Stores tab renders the store list via renderStoresTab().
Store data is fetched alongside other config data in the Promise.all() call.
Switching away from the Stores tab resets module state and closes any open modal.

summary: WP-008 PASS. Zero-change WP — all 6 integration ACs were satisfied by prior WP-006 work. Source review of config.js confirms: configActiveTab defaults to 'general' (line 14, hard-coded at declaration); Stores tab button is first in the tab bar template; renderConfigTabContent() dispatches the stores case to renderStoresTab()+csWireEvents(); API.getStores is guarded with a presence ternary that safely degrades to Promise.resolve([]) on missing method; tab-switch cleanup at lines 94-104 unconditionally resets all cs* module state, removes the delegated click listener, and calls csCloseModal(); configDirty initialised with stores: false in the chained assignment at line 52.
The API.getStores presence check and the duplicated reset logic across the two cleanup sites are both low-priority observations that don’t affect correctness. No files modified.

comments.note: configActiveTab defaults to 'general' at declaration (config.js line 14) — not a flag or runtime default, it is hard-coded. This means the default tab cannot be changed via configuration; it is a code-level invariant. Correct for current requirements, but worth noting if future work ever needs a configurable default tab.

API.getStores ? API.getStores() : Promise.resolve([]) — the ternary guard is a correct defensive pattern for SPA deployment safety (protects against loading a cached config.js against an older api-client.js without the method). The silent empty-list fallback is intentional. Since config-stores.js is declared as a prerequisite in config.js's module comment, the guard is belt-and-suspenders rather than load-order management.

Tab-switch cleanup (lines 94-104) and fresh-load block in renderConfigPage() (lines 52-59) both reset csStores, csOriginal, csReorderMode, csModalMode, csModalStoreId, csModalCreateDir, and call csCloseModal(). The two sites differ only in csClickHandler handling: fresh-load sets it to null without DOM removal (entire DOM is replaced); tab-switch explicitly removes the listener before nulling. A csResetModuleState() helper could eliminate the duplication, but the two cleanup paths must remain semantically separate — flagging as tech debt, not a Fix-Forward.

No code changes were made in this WP. Zero-change WP has no artifact files to review — all 6 ACs verified by source inspection of the existing integration code in config.js and index.html. QA's observation about absence of runtime testing is accurate; the integration was implicitly tested by the regression suite run during WP-006 and WP-007.
